NONE: › a child or animal without a home or enough food and care, usually thin and dirty in appearance
（通常指又瘦又髒的）流浪兒；無家可歸的小動物
› very thin and delicate in appearance
瘦弱的；弱不禁風的
› people with no homes
無家可歸者

example: Her house is always full of waifs and strays.
她的房子裡總是住滿無家可歸的人。

I or T: › [ I or T ] to make a long, high cry, usually because of pain or sadness
I: › [ I ] informal to complain loudly or strongly

NONE: › a long, high, loud cry, especially because of something unpleasant
慟哭；號啕大哭

example: The women gathered around the coffin and began to wail, as was the custom in the region.
女人們都圍到了棺材旁，開始號啕大哭，當地的風俗就是這樣。
[ + speech ] "My finger hurts," wailed the child.
「我的手指頭很痛，」那個孩子大哭道。
[ + that ] Business people wailed that their trade would be ruined.
生意人都強烈抱怨說他們的買賣會被毀掉的。
a wail of anguish
痛苦的哀號
the wail of the police sirens
警笛的尖嘯聲

NONE: B2 the part of the body above and slightly narrower than the hips
腰，腰部
› the part of a piece of clothing that goes around or covers the area between the hips and the ribs
（衣服的）腰部

example: a small/narrow/tiny/large/thick waist
小／窄／極細的／寬／粗腰
These trousers are a bit tight around my waist.
這條褲子我穿著腰有點緊。
The skirt had an elasticated waist.
這條裙子的腰部是鬆緊性的。

NONE: › a
bumbag
› a strip of material that forms the waist of a pair of trousers or a skirt
褲帶；裙帶

example: He had a gun tucked into the waistband of his trousers.
他腰帶上塞了一把槍。

NONE: › a piece of clothing that covers the upper body but not the arms and usually has buttons down the front, worn over a shirt
西服背心；馬夾
› having a particular type of waist
有…腰身的
› narrower at the waist or in the middle
（衣服）有腰身的，收腰的
› used with adjectives to describe the type of waist that a person or piece of clothing has
（與形容詞搭配，表示一個人或一件衣服的）…腰身

example: high/low waisted jeans
高／低腰牛仔褲
a thick waisted middle-aged man
一名粗腰的中年男人
The coats were old-fashioned in cut, waisted and full skirted.
這些大衣採用的是老式裁剪，收腰、全長下擺。
a slim-waisted boy
細腰的男孩
a high-waisted pair of trousers
一條高腰褲

NONE: › an imaginary line going round the narrowest part of your waist
腰圍；腰圍線

example: a bulging/expanding waistline
日益變粗／逐漸變大的腰圍
She started jogging twice a week to try to reduce her waistline.
她開始一週慢跑兩次，希望能瘦腰。

NONE: A1 to allow time to go by, especially while staying in one place without doing very much, until someone comes, until something that you are expecting happens or until you can do something
等待，等候；期盼，盼望
› to be done or to happen at a later time
延後；耽擱
B2 a period of time when you stay in one place until someone comes, or something happens, or until you can do something
等待；等候，期待
› used on signs to mean vehicles are not allowed to park, even for short periods of time
禁止停車

example: I waited for her outside while she went in to see the doctor.
她進去看病時，我在外面等她。
The dentist kept me waiting for ages.
牙醫讓我等了好久。
[ + to infinitive ] There were a lot of people waiting to use the phone.
有很多人在等著打電話。
The meeting will have to wait until tomorrow, because I'm too busy now.
會議將不得不延後到明天，因為我現在太忙了。
The paperwork can't wait until tomorrow (= is urgent and must be done now).
這些文書工作不能等到明天再做。
The sign by the side of the road said "no waiting!"
路邊的標誌牌上寫著「禁止停車」。
We had a three-hour wait before we could see the doctor.
我們等了三個小時才看到醫生。
The long wait for the doctor/to see the doctor really made me anxious.
等醫生看病等了那麼長時間真讓我焦急。

NONE: B1 said in order to interrupt someone or to get their attention, or when you have suddenly thought of something important
等等，等一下（用於突然想起某件重要的事時）

example: Now, wait a moment - I don't agree with that.
喂，等等——我不同意那樣做。
Wait a minute - I've just had an idea.
等一下——我剛想出個主意。

NONE: C1 to wait to discover what will happen
等等看；等著瞧

example: No decision will be made until next year, so you'll just have to wait and see.
得等到明年才會有決定，所以你只好等等看了。

NONE: › to stay in a place and do nothing while you wait for someone to arrive or something to happen
無所事事地等

example: We spent the whole day waiting around for something exciting to happen, but nothing did.
我們白白等了一整天，指望有甚麼激動人心的事發生，結果甚麼也沒有。

NONE: › to serve meals to people in a restaurant, as your job
（在餐館）當侍者
› UK to stay in a place after all the other people have left
留下來不走

example: The teacher made us wait behind after class.
老師讓我們課後留下來不要走。

NONE: › used to show that you are about to say something surprising, funny, or difficult to believe
（表示將要說某些驚人、可笑或令人難以置信的事）聽著，聽好了
› UK used to tell someone not to not start until the correct moment
等一等

example: Depending on who you believe, the problem is either too much political interference or - wait for it - not enough.
這就取決於你相信誰了，問題要麼是太多政治干涉，要麼——聽好了——干涉不夠。
Wait for it! I haven't said "go" yet.
等一等！我還沒說「開始」呢。

NONE: › If something is waiting for you, it has been left or prepared for you to collect, use, enjoy, or deal with when you arrive.
等著（某人）去做（或處理等）

example: An envelope was waiting for me when I got home.
我到家時看到有我的一封信。
Uma had a cup of coffee waiting for me, along with a plate of biscuits.
烏馬泡了一杯茶等我喝，還準備了一盤餅乾。

NONE: › to be expecting someone or something and be prepared to deal with him, her, or it
等待…，等著…

example: When the thieves left the building, the police were waiting for them.
當盜賊們離開那棟樓的時候，警察正在等著抓他們。

NONE: › to stay at home because you are expecting someone or something to arrive, or someone to phone you
在家裡等待

example: I waited in for the plumber all morning, but he didn't turn up.
我在家裡等那個水管工等了一上午，可他卻連面也沒露。

NONE: › If someone or something is waiting in the wings, they are not yet active or important, but are ready or likely to be so soon.
準備就緒；隨時可使用

example: The team has several talented young players waiting in the wings.
這支隊伍裡有幾位很有天賦的年輕隊員隨時可以頂替。

NONE: › to do everything for someone so that that person does not have to do anything for himself or herself
服侍，伺候

example: While she was pregnant, her husband waited on her hand and foot (= did everything for her).
她懷孕時，她丈夫無微不至地照顧她。

NONE: › to serve food and drink, especially to customers in a restaurant
（尤指在餐館裡）服侍…進餐，給…上菜

example: The staff who waited on us at dinner were excellent.
吃飯時為我們服務的侍者非常不錯。
She waited on tables (= served meals as a job) to earn some extra money.
她當侍者來賺些額外的收入。

NONE: › to wait until you know the result of an activity before doing or deciding something
等待，等候

example: The lawyers are waiting on the jury's verdict.
律師們在等待陪審團的裁決。

NONE: › to delay serving a meal until someone arrives
等候（某人吃飯）

example: Don't wait dinner for me - I'll be home late.
別等我吃飯了——我會很晚才回家。

NONE: › to wait until something unpleasant has ended
等到（令人不快之事）結束

example: I'd rather wait out the storm than drive home immediately.
我想等到風暴過去，而不是馬上開車回家。

NONE: › said when you are excited about seeing another person's reaction to something special or unusual
等到…吧（表示對看到某人對某些特別或不尋常之事的反應感到興奮）

example: Wait till you see what Rachel's wearing!
看看瑞秋的穿著你會大吃一驚的！
Wait till he hears the news.
等著看他聽到這則消息後會有甚麼反應吧。

NONE: › to not go to bed at night because you are expecting someone to arrive
（晚上）不睡覺（等某人回家）

example: I'll be home after midnight, so don't wait up for me.
我會在半夜以後才回家，所以你先睡吧，不用等我。

NONE: › to wait until it is really your turn to do or get something
等著輪到你

example: If people were more polite, they would wait their turn.
假如人們是更講禮貌的話，他們就會按順序等候。

NONE: A1 a man whose job is to bring the food to customers at their tables in a restaurant
（餐館的）男侍者，男服務員
› a situation in which you delay taking any action, so that you can watch how a situation develops and see what it is best for you to do
伺機而動的策略

example: In a contest like this, the stronger team can afford to play a waiting game.
在這種比賽中，實力較強的一方才可以採取伺機而動的策略。

NONE: › a list of people who have asked for something that is not immediately available but will be in the future
等候者名單

example: The hospital has a two-year waiting list for minor operations.
這家醫院的小手術已經排到了兩年後。
The course is full, but I can put you on the waiting list, in case someone drops out.
這門課程已經滿額了，但我可以把你列在後補名單裡，說不定有人會放棄。

NONE: › a room in a place where people can sit while waiting, as in an airport or a doctor's office
等候室；候車室；候診室
A1 a woman whose job is to bring the food to customers at their tables in a restaurant
（餐館裡的）女侍者，女服務員
› to not demand something you have a right to, or not cause a rule to be obeyed
放棄（權利）；不遵守（規則）

example: The bank manager waived the charge (= said we didn't have to pay), as we were old and valued customers.
那位銀行經理沒有收取我們的費用，因為我們是尊貴的老顧客。
If they waive (= remove) the time limit, many more applications will come in.
假如取消時間限制，那麼就會收到多得多的申請。
He persuaded the delegates to waive (= give up) their objections.
他說服代表們不再反對。

NONE: › an agreement that you do not have to pay or obey something
免支付協議；棄權聲明書

example: We had to sign a waiver, giving up any rights to the land in the future.
我們不得不簽了一份棄權聲明，放棄將來對那塊土地的任何權利。
